title_en: Wonders of Chinese Engineering (20/20): An Automated Container Terminal
note_en: 着 (zhe) after a verb marks an ongoing action or state that forms the backdrop of a scene: 巨大的桥吊和轨道吊安静地装卸着集装箱 "giant cranes are quietly loading and unloading containers." English uses "-ing" for this, but Chinese verbs don't change form, so 着 does the job; it is especially common in descriptive writing that paints a picture rather than reports events.
